name: John Watson
description: John Watson, a Black grocer and confectioner in Oberlin, Ohio, was one of the twenty men committed to the Cuyahoga County Jail for the 1858 Oberlin–Wellington Rescue of John Price, a freedom-seeker seized under the Fugitive Slave Act. He refused release on recognizance and remained jailed from April 15 until the mass discharge on July 6, 1859.

cases.convicted: No — indictment dismissed July 6, 1859, when the Rescue charges were dropped in exchange for dismissal of the Ohio kidnapping case against Price's captors.
cases.sentence: Held April 15 – July 6, 1859 (about 82 days); no conviction.

name: John Mandeville
description: John Mandeville was a defendant in the 1858 Oberlin–Wellington Rescue of the freedom-seeker John Price. On May 6, 1859 he was sentenced to 24 hours in the county jail, a 20-dollar fine and costs; the marshal treated the limits of Cleveland as the boundary of the "jail," so the custody was largely nominal rather than physical confinement in a cell.

cases.convicted: Yes — sentenced May 6, 1859 to 24 hours, a 20-dollar fine and costs.
cases.sentence: 24-hour sentence (May 6–7, 1859); the marshal treated the Cleveland city limits as the jail, so custody was largely nominal.
